subject: Deployment provenance and license schedule — Helix Health on-prem pilot
messages:
From: Samantha Lee <samantha.lee@helixhealth.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene@redwood.com>
Cc: procurements@helixhealth.com
Date: 2026-07-09T09:12:00Z
Subject: Deployment provenance & license questions for on-prem pilot

Hi Irene,

Thanks again for the walkthrough yesterday. We're moving toward an on-prem pilot (non-production) and legal asked for a short schedule and the exact list of "deployment provenance" items Redwood can provide for a phased evidence handoff. Specifically they want to understand:
- What is the license surface for the on-prem image vs. hosted model (what is allowed/disallowed)?
- Operator access model: will we get operator console credentials, or is there a guarded jump-host process?
- What artifacts can be provided as proof of deployment: e.g., signed image checksums, snapshot manifests, runbook excerpts, audit log extracts, or a notarized escrow-style snapshot?
- Typical time to produce these artifacts and a suggested calendar for the pilot (we'd like to start staging the week of 7/20).

I've attached our PO (po-45721.pdf) for reference. Legal also flagged export control / IP boundary language — they want to see an example of the proposed MSA exhibit and any proposed limited-license paragraph we should expect.

Could you send a short plan (1 page) and a checklist that we can share with our counsel by EOD Monday?

Best,
Samantha
Samantha Lee
Head of Cloud Integrations, Helix Health
-- attachment: po-45721.pdf (application/pdf) --

From: Irene Choi <irene@redwood.com>
To: Samantha Lee <samantha.lee@helixhealth.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-07-09T11:03:00Z
Subject: Re: Deployment provenance & license questions for on-prem pilot

Samantha — thanks for the clear list. High level response and next steps below. I'll also attach our latest MSA redlines and a draft evidence matrix for Helix.

Summary (short):
- License surface: for on-prem pilot we propose a "restricted runtime license" that permits inference in-scoped for Helix internal apps only; model weights remain Redwood-owned under a limited redistribution prohibition; details in attached redlines (see section: Licensed Use & Redistribution).
- Operator access: two modes supported — (1) console operator (Redwood-managed) with session recording or (2) customer-managed operator with jump-host + role-limited accounts. For pilots we typically offer option (2) with time-boxed operator accounts and SSO integration.
- Artifacts we can provide: signed image checksum (SHA256), snapshot manifest (manifest.json stub), audit log extracts (sample CSV), runbook excerpt (PDF), and a sealed checksum delivered to counsel on acceptance. We do not push full model weights into escrow as a routine; we can discuss an agreed escrow-lite arrangement with a third-party custodian if required.
- Timing: we can produce a draft evidence matrix and provisional runbook excerpt within 3 business days; checksum and snapshot manifest within 7 business days; full audit extracts per agreed window (typically monthly).

Proposed immediate actions (please confirm):
1) Helix confirms pilot start week (you suggested week of 7/20).
2) Helix confirms preferred operator access mode (Redwood-managed limited access or customer jump-host).
3) We exchange NDA/limited exhibit if you want the MSA exhibit early (we have an internal redline v3 attached).

Attachments: redwood-MSA-redlines_v3.pdf, evidence-matrix_helix.xlsx (draft)

I'll loop in Karthik for the final evidence checklist and Laura for legal boundary language.

Thanks —
Irene Choi
Head, Customer Security & Deployments
Redwood Inference
-- attachments: redwood-MSA-redlines_v3.pdf (application/pdf), evidence-matrix_helix.xlsx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet) --

From: Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>
To: Samantha Lee <samantha@helixhealth.com>
Cc: Irene Choi <irene@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-07-09T13:28:00Z
Subject: Re: Deployment provenance & license questions for on-prem pilot

Samantha — quick legal note.

Two things to highlight that Helix counsel often raises:
- IP boundary: we can carve a limited license to run the service in your environment but we will keep ownership of model weights and derivative IP. We can propose a narrow clause that prohibits redistribution and derivative-model commercialization.
- Escrow-like options: we offer an "escrow-lite" exhibit — not full source/material escrow — that defines the triggers, custodian roles, and an evidence delivery path (checksums, manifests, and operator attestation). If you need full source escrow (weights + training code) that becomes an exceptional request and will require legal/finance review.

Operational asks for Helix to confirm:
- Audit window (preferred dates for log extracts)
- Whether audit evidence should be delivered to internal Helix counsel or an external third-party custodian

If Helix is comfortable with the escrow-lite pathway we can start drafting the exhibit now; otherwise flag and we'll prepare an MSA amendment template for heavier custody.

I'll schedule a 30m call with legal + ops tomorrow to walk the redlines if that works — proposed times attached in the calendar invite.

Laura Bennett
Deputy General Counsel, Redwood Inference
-- calendar invite: redlines-legal-sync.ics (text/calendar) --

From: Samantha Lee <samantha.lee@helixhealth.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>, Irene Choi <irene@redwood.com>
Cc: procurements@helixhealth.com
Date: 2026-07-10T08:45:00Z
Subject: Re: Deployment provenance & license questions for on-prem pilot

Laura / Irene — thanks, that helps. A few quick confirmations: 
- Helix prefers the escrow-lite pathway for the pilot. Our counsel wants the evidence delivered to an agreed third-party custodian (we can propose one).
- Pilot staging week: 2026-07-20 (we can accept runbook excerpts and the draft evidence matrix before then).
- Operator access: we'll take the customer jump-host model for staging, and we'll revisit console operator mode for production.

Question: for the sealed checksum, will Redwood provide a signed checksum image and manifest that we can store with our counsel? Also, can you include a sample audit log extract for a 24-hour window so our security team can validate format?

Attaching the PO and the Helix counsel contact card for the custodian conversation.

Samantha
-- attachment: po-45721.pdf (application/pdf) --

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
To: Samantha Lee <samantha@helixhealth.com>
Cc: Irene Choi <irene@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-07-11T15:46:00Z
Subject: Re: Deployment provenance & license questions for on-prem pilot

Samantha — thanks, all good. Operational plan below (concise):

1) Deliverables & timing
- Day 0 (upon PO acceptance): deliver redlines summary and draft evidence matrix (we will deliver updated evidence-matrix_helix.xlsx).
- Day 3: runbook excerpt (procedural snippets for deployment, restart, and incident contact list).
- Day 7: signed image checksum (SHA256) and snapshot manifest (manifest.json stub) delivered to Helix counsel and the named custodian.
- Day 10: sample audit log extract (24-hour window) and a session-recording excerpt (redacted) for format validation.

2) Access model
- Jump-host approach: Helix ops will provide the bastion IP list and we will provide short-lived, role-limited accounts (mfa + tfa enforced). All sessions will be recorded and checksummed daily.

3) Evidence handling
- We will produce signed artifacts (PDF summary with RSA signature), and we can also deliver a sealed GPG-signed tarball to the third-party custodian if needed. We recommend the escrow-lite trigger be custody-of-evidence + joint-counsel verification.

4) Next steps (action items)
- Samantha: confirm custodian name and contact (if you have one) and confirm staging date of 7/20.
- Helix counsel: confirm if signed checksum is acceptable form-factor or if notarization is required.
- Redwood (Marissa): prepare the DRAFT exhibit clause for escrow-lite and propose a limited-license paragraph for Helix counsel to review.

I'll attach the updated evidence matrix and a sample manifest after this message. If you'd like a quick call Wednesday morning (US-PST) to walk through the manifest format, we can do 9:30am PT.

Thanks,
Karthik Iyer
Sr. Manager, Deployment Engineering
Redwood Inference
-- attachments: evidence-matrix_helix_v2.xlsx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet), sample-manifest.json (application/json) --
